title: Vaneaxial Fan Parts
description: FanPedia's exploded views of direct drive and belt driven vaneaxial fans (p. 16) with eleven numbered markers, leader lines and two label columns. Explore mode previews each part's name and description; quiz mode hides the labels and describes each part by its job or look, with two attempts, a hint after the first miss and mastery at 9 of 11 on the first attempt.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Parts of direct drive and belt driven vaneaxial fans
learningObjectives: The learner will identify the eleven labeled parts of direct drive and belt driven vaneaxial fans on FanPedia's exploded views, given each part's function or appearance.

accessibility.notes: The drawing is a labelled SVG group; every numbered marker is a focusable role=button and Tab walks them in number order; Enter or Space selects one; focus or hover previews its name and description. During the quiz the markers are named only 'Part n' until resolved, labels and leader lines are hidden, and hints never name the answer. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live). ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and an 'Answer' badge pair with colour. Text is 12 px or larger; markers keep a constant pixel size; the two label columns move below the drawing as a numbered list on screens narrower than 820 px.

simulation.modelType: labeled diagram with locate quiz (FP.Overlay callout engine on FP.CalloutQuiz)
rules: Explore mode: hover or focus previews a part's name and description; click, Enter or Space opens it and counts it as visited; never scored.
Quiz mode: 11 prompts in a seeded shuffle (the same order for every learner; Start over reshuffles).
Two attempts per prompt; the first wrong answer shows a hint that does not name the answer; the second reveals the answer and counts as missed.
Selecting empty space uses no attempt.
Only first-attempt answers count toward mastery; mastery is 9 of 11.
assumptions: FanPedia p. 16 exploded views (direct drive vaneaxial fans on the left, belt driven vaneaxial fans on the right), with the printed labels removed; marker positions are percentages of the image.
limitations: The drawings are FanPedia's, not a specific current catalog model; the two belt driven views were moved closer to the direct drive views to close the empty middle of the page (layout only).

sources: FanPedia p. 16 (Exploded Views: Axial Fans, 'Direct Drive Vaneaxial Fans' and 'Belt Driven Vaneaxial Fans'): drawing and part names
FanPedia pp. 15-16 (exploded views of axial fans) and Chapter 4 sections 'Axial Fans', 'Tubular Housings' and 'Guide Vanes': descriptions
Drawing: FanPedia, Twin City Fan, p. 16

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore labelled markers on the real FanPedia drawing first, then retrieval practice: find each part from a description of its job, with a hint after the first miss and immediate correction.
keyQuestions: What does a vaneaxial fan have that a tubeaxial fan does not, and what does it do to the air?
Where does the motor sit on a direct drive axial fan, and where on a belt driven one?
commonMisconceptions: A vaneaxial fan differs from a tubeaxial fan only in its impeller.
The guide vanes rotate with the impeller.
A belt driven axial fan has its motor in the airstream.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 11'; mastery is 9 of 11 on the first attempt.
